articles.title: Effects of Bispectral Index monitoring on ambulatory anesthesia: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and a cost analysis.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring is increasingly used to titrate anesthetics in ambulatory surgery, where rapid recovery and discharge matter.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: We pooled randomized controlled trials comparing BIS-guided with standard anesthetic practice in ambulatory patients and estimated the costs involved.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: Across the included trials, BIS guidance modestly reduced anesthetic use, the risk of nausea and vomiting, and time spent in the recovery room, but not total time in the ambulatory unit.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: BIS monitoring produced small reductions in anesthetic consumption, postoperative nausea and vomiting, and recovery room time. The cost of the electrode outweighed any savings.

articles.title: Inadequate emergence after anesthesia: emergence delirium and hypoactive emergence in the Postanesthesia Care Unit.

abstract_parts.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract_parts.text: To describe how often inadequate emergence occurs after elective surgery in the Postanesthesia Care Unit (PACU), with its determinants and consequences.

abstract_parts.label: DESIGN
abstract_parts.text: Prospective observational study.

abstract_parts.label: SETTING
abstract_parts.text: PACU of a university hospital.

abstract_parts.label: PATIENTS
abstract_parts.text: Adults recovering from general anesthesia.

abstract_parts.label: MEASUREMENTS
abstract_parts.text: Emergence delirium and hypoactive emergence were assessed with a sedation-agitation scale on PACU admission and at discharge.

abstract_parts.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: Inadequate emergence was common. Emergence delirium was associated with higher pain scores and longer preoperative fasting, whereas hypoactive emergence was associated with longer stays.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: Higher postoperative pain and longer fasting were preventable determinants of emergence delirium. Hypoactive emergence was linked to longer PACU and hospital stays.

articles.title: Effect of Electroencephalography-Guided Anesthetic Administration on Postoperative Delirium Among Older Adults Undergoing Major Surgery: The ENGAGES Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract_parts.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract_parts.text: Intraoperative EEG suppression, a possible marker of excessive anesthetic depth, has been associated with postoperative delirium.

abstract_parts.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract_parts.text: To test whether EEG-guided anesthetic administration reduces postoperative delirium in older adults.

abstract_parts.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract_parts.text: Pragmatic randomized clinical trial of older adults undergoing major elective surgery at one academic medical center.

abstract_parts.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract_parts.text: Patients were randomly assigned to EEG-guided anesthetic administration or usual care.

abstract_parts.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract_parts.text: The primary outcome was delirium on postoperative days 1 to 5; adverse events included intraoperative movement and hypotension.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: EEG guidance reduced EEG suppression and anesthetic exposure, but delirium incidence did not differ between groups. Serious adverse events were similar in both groups.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract_parts.text: Among older adults undergoing major surgery, EEG-guided anesthetic administration did not decrease the incidence of postoperative delirium compared with usual care. These findings do not support EEG guidance for this indication.

abstract_parts.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract_parts.text: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02241655.

articles.title: Association of electroencephalogram trajectories during emergence from anaesthesia with delirium in the postanaesthesia care unit: an early sign of postoperative complications.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Delirium in the postanaesthesia care unit (PACU) may herald later postoperative complications.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: Frontal EEG was recorded during emergence from general anaesthesia in adults, and emergence trajectories were classified from their spectral patterns.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: Patients whose emergence lacked a slow-wave pattern more often developed PACU delirium, which was associated with a longer hospital stay.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: Specific EEG trajectories during emergence were associated with PACU delirium. Such patterns may help predict delirium and point to targets for prevention.

articles.title: Bispectral index for improving intraoperative awareness and early postoperative recovery in adults.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Clinical signs and end-tidal anaesthetic gas may not reliably reflect hypnotic depth during anaesthesia.

abstract_parts.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract_parts.text: To assess BIS-guided anaesthesia for preventing intraoperative awareness and improving early recovery.

abstract_parts.label: SEARCH METHODS
abstract_parts.text: We searched major databases and trial registers.

abstract_parts.label: SELECTION CRITERIA
abstract_parts.text: Randomized controlled trials comparing BIS-guided anaesthesia with clinical signs or end-tidal gas monitoring.

abstract_parts.label: DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS
abstract_parts.text: Two authors independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias.

abstract_parts.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: BIS guidance may reduce awareness compared with clinical signs and modestly shorten times to eye opening and PACU discharge, with low-certainty evidence.

abstract_parts.label: AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: Awareness during anaesthesia is uncommon, and the evidence that BIS guidance prevents it remains imprecise. BIS may modestly improve early recovery times.

articles.title: Bispectral Index (BIS) Monitoring and Postoperative Delirium in Elderly Patients Undergoing Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

abstract_parts.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract_parts.text: To examine whether BIS-guided anesthesia lowers postoperative delirium in elderly surgical patients.

abstract_parts.label: DESIGN
abstract_parts.text: A systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis.

abstract_parts.label: SETTING
abstract_parts.text: Randomized trials identified in electronic databases.

abstract_parts.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract_parts.text: Elderly patients undergoing surgery.

abstract_parts.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract_parts.text: BIS-guided versus usual anesthetic care.

abstract_parts.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: BIS guidance did not significantly reduce delirium but was associated with less postoperative cognitive dysfunction and faster recovery.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSION
abstract_parts.text: In this meta-analysis, BIS-guided anesthesia was not associated with fewer cases of postoperative delirium, although it was associated with less postoperative cognitive dysfunction and better recovery parameters.

articles.title: Preoperative characterization of baseline EEG recordings for risk stratification of post-anesthesia care unit delirium.

abstract_parts.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract_parts.text: Delirium in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU-D) is a frequent complication in older surgical patients.

abstract_parts.label: DESIGN AND SETTING
abstract_parts.text: Post-hoc analysis of preoperative EEG recordings in patients with and without PACU-D.

abstract_parts.label: PATIENTS AND MEASUREMENTS
abstract_parts.text: Baseline EEG was recorded with eyes open and closed, and spectral and entropy measures were compared.

abstract_parts.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: Patients who developed PACU-D showed different baseline spectral power and entropy patterns.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: Baseline EEG recorded before surgery may help stratify the risk of PACU delirium after general anesthesia. Routine monitoring parameters captured these differences.

abstract_parts.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract_parts.text: DRKS registration.

articles.title: Electroencephalographic Biomarkers, Cerebral Oximetry, and Postoperative Cognitive Function in Adult Noncardiac Surgical Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Neurophysiologic biomarkers that predict cognition after surgery are lacking.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: Single-center prospective observational study recording multichannel EEG and cerebral oximetry before, during and after noncardiac surgery.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: Preoperative posterior alpha power and frontal-parietal connectivity did not correlate with postoperative cognitive scores.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: Preoperative alpha power, connectivity and cerebral oximetry were not associated with cognitive function after noncardiac surgery.

articles.title: Predictors of Low Risk for Delirium during Anesthesia Emergence.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Processed EEG may predict delirium, but emergence trajectories of EEG band power are rarely used clinically.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: Data from a previously published study were reanalyzed, and frontal EEG power slopes during emergence were modeled.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: Steeper changes in specific frequency bands during emergence identified patients at low risk for delirium.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: A simple analysis of one frontal EEG channel identified emergence patterns typical of patients at low risk for delirium.

articles.title: Bispectral Index Monitoring Effect on Delirium Occurrence and Nursing Quality Improvement in Post-anesthesia Care Unit Patients Recovering From General Anesthesia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Whether monitoring anesthetic depth affects delirium and nursing quality in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) is unclear.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: This randomized controlled trial included 120 adults; one group received BIS-guided anesthesia and the other usual care.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: BIS guidance was associated with fewer adverse events and less delirium in the PACU, and with better nursing quality scores.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSION
abstract_parts.text: Intraoperative BIS monitoring may reduce adverse events and delirium in the PACU and lessen the nursing workload.

articles.title: The Impact of Anesthetic Management Under Bispectral Index Monitoring on the Early Recovery Quality of Elderly Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Surgery: A Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract_parts.label: PURPOSE
abstract_parts.text: To evaluate BIS-guided anesthetic depth and early recovery quality in elderly laparoscopic patients.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: Ninety patients aged 60 years or older were randomized into empirical, BIS 40-60 and BIS 50-60 groups.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: BIS-guided groups had better early recovery scores and fewer adverse events than the empirical group.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSION
abstract_parts.text: BIS-guided anesthesia management may improve early recovery after laparoscopic surgery in elderly patients.

articles.title: EEG alpha power and delirium in the postanaesthesia care unit in older adults: the AlphaMax trial part 2 - effect of propofol infusion during emergence from desflurane anaesthesia<sup>☆</sup>.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: This arm of the AlphaMax trial tested a short propofol infusion at the end of surgery during emergence in older adults.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: Patients were randomly assigned to propofol or placebo infusion during emergence from desflurane anaesthesia.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: Propofol reduced alpha power and increased burst suppression during emergence; PACU delirium did not differ.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: Propofol infusion lowered EEG alpha power during emergence, but the incidence of PACU delirium was unchanged.

abstract_parts.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract_parts.text: ACTRN registration.

articles.title: EEG alpha power and delirium in the postanaesthesia care unit in older adults: the AlphaMax trial part 1 - effect of desflurane and fentanyl titration during maintenance.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Frontal EEG alpha oscillations may indicate adequate anaesthesia with antinociception, and low alpha power marks a vulnerable brain.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: Older adults were randomly assigned to EEG-guided titration of desflurane and fentanyl or to usual care.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: EEG guidance slightly increased alpha power without differences in delirium or other clinical outcomes.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: EEG-guided titration of fentanyl and desflurane had only a small effect on alpha power and no appreciable effect on clinical outcomes.

abstract_parts.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract_parts.text: ACTRN registration.

articles.title: Processed electroencephalogram-guided anesthesia and its impact on postoperative delirium and perioperative efficiency: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract_parts.label: BACKGROUND
abstract_parts.text: Processed EEG (pEEG) indices are recommended for monitoring anesthetic depth.

abstract_parts.label: METHODS
abstract_parts.text: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing pEEG-guided with non-guided anesthesia.

abstract_parts.label: RESULTS
abstract_parts.text: pEEG guidance reduced anesthetic use, shortened wake-up and PACU times, and lowered postoperative delirium.

abstract_parts.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract_parts.text: Across many randomized trials, pEEG-guided anesthesia improved perioperative efficiency and reduced postoperative delirium. Evidence is strongest for BIS.
